sentences.text: Brodavis is a genus of freshwater birds belonging to the order Hesperornithiformes.
This animal is considered the first freshwater species and the latest known record of its order.
Although flight was likely lost by the end of the Early Cretaceous, minimal bone density in Brodavis suggests the possibility of some flying ability.
The genus was first described and named by Larry D. Martin, Evgeny N. Kurochkin, and Tim T. Tokaryk in 2012.
The type species Brodavis americanus is known from a holotype left metatarsal collected in the Maastrichtian-age Frenchman Formation of Canada.
Brodavis baileyi is known from a holotype left metatarsal collected in the Maastrichtian-age Hell Creek Formation of South Dakota, dated between 66.8 and 66 million years ago.
Brodavis mongoliensis is known from a holotype left metatarsal collected in the Maastrichtian-age Nemegt Formation of Mongolia.
Brodavis varneri was originally named as a species of Baptornis by James Martin and Amanda Cordes-Person in 2007.
Brodavis was assigned to a new monogeneric family called Brodavidae.
Fossils of Brodavis are known from the Late Cretaceous, possibly the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages, in North America and Asia.
Brodavis lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
It is debated whether Baptornis varneri represents a fourth species of Brodavis or belongs to a separate genus.
